Thank you all for the thorough updates. Let me address each item and give you clear direction on sequencing.

First, Marcus — the conflicts issue is our top priority. You're right that we cannot proceed without informed written consent from both clients and a documented ethical screen. Please start drafting the informed consent disclosures and ethical screen documentation today. I'll need you to document the required safeguard in the engagement memo as well. Once you have those drafts ready, we'll need to coordinate outreach to the opposing party's relationship partner for their consent. If we cannot secure consent from both sides, we will not take this engagement — that's non-negotiable.

Second, Nadia — thank you for the preliminary findings. Since the conflicts issue may be dispositive, I agree it makes sense to hold your full patent litigation analysis until we know whether we can clear the conflicts hurdle. However, your recommendation that the invalidity defense be limited to claim 7 based on the pre-critical-date publication is noted. Please circulate your research note to the intake group so we have it on file, and be prepared to build out the litigation plan if and when we clear conflicts.

Third, Tom — the $300,000 total-fee cap through trial is a significant constraint. I need you to enter that instruction in the client-relations record today so it's properly documented. We'll need to assess whether a patent infringement defense through trial can realistically be handled within that cap, and Nadia's recommendation to limit the invalidity defense to claim 7 may actually help us manage scope and cost. That fee cap will need to be reflected explicitly in the engagement letter.

So the sequence is: (1) Marcus drafts consent disclosures and ethical screen documentation and documents the safeguard in the engagement memo; (2) we coordinate consent from the opposing party's relationship partner; (3) once conflicts are cleared, Nadia circulates her research note and we finalize the litigation plan scoped to claim 7; and (4) Tom documents the fee cap and we incorporate all terms into the engagement letter by Wednesday. If Marcus cannot secure consent from both clients, we decline the engagement. Questions?
